items.title: Relative pseudo-coherence is local for a cover by principal opens of the algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a finite type map and elements generating the unit ideal of the algebra, relative pseudo-coherence of a complex is equivalent to relative pseudo-coherence of each of its localizations at those elements, and the same for pseudo-coherence (statement lines 21668-21681). One implication is the localization statement, while the converse requires presenting the algebra by a polynomial ring in the elements and their complementary coefficients modulo the relation expressing the partition of unity, checking that this presentation is pseudo-coherent over the polynomial ring, and then transferring relative pseudo-coherence from the localized algebras up to the polynomial ring and back, using the glueing statement along the way (proof lines 21683-21711). The presentation and the two transfers are what turn a local hypothesis into a global conclusion. The counted span refers three times to earlier results of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
